column3: Then he told them a parable about the need for them always to pray and not lose heart,
saying, “There was a judge in a certain city who did not fear God and did not respect people.
There was also a widow in that city, and she kept coming to him, saying, ‘Give me justice against my opponent.’
For a time he was unwilling, but afterward he said to himself, ‘Even though I do not fear God or respect people,
yet because this widow keeps causing me trouble, I will give her justice, so that she does not keep coming and wear me out.’”
Then the Lord said, “Listen to what the unrighteous judge says.
And will God not bring about justice for his chosen ones who cry out to him day and night? Will he delay long over them?
I tell you, he will bring about justice for them quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”
He also told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and treated the rest with contempt:
“Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood and prayed these things to himself: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like the rest of people—swindlers, unrighteous, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week; I give a tenth of everything I acquire.’
But the tax collector, standing far away, would not even lift his eyes to heaven, but was beating his chest, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, the sinner!’
I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
Now people were bringing even infants to him so that he might touch them. When the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
But Jesus called them to him, saying, “Allow the children to come to me and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will certainly not enter it.”
And a certain ruler asked him, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery; do not murder; do not steal; do not bear false witness; honor your father and mother.”
He said, “I have kept all these from my youth.”
When Jesus heard this, he said to him, “One thing you still lack: sell everything you have, distribute it to the poor, and you will have treasure in the heavens; then come, follow me.”
But when he heard these things, he became deeply sorrowful, because he was extremely rich.
Jesus, seeing him become sorrowful, said, “How difficult it is for those who have riches to enter the kingdom of God!
For it is easier for a camel to enter through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
Those who heard it said, “Then who can be saved?”
He said, “The things impossible with people are possible with God.”
Peter said, “Look, we have left what was ours and followed you.”
He said to them, “Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
who will not receive many times more in this time, and in the coming age eternal life.”
Then taking the twelve aside, he said to them, “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything written through the prophets about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.
For he will be handed over to the Gentiles, mocked, mistreated, and spit upon.
After flogging him, they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise.”
But they understood none of these things. This saying was hidden from them, and they did not grasp what was being said.
Now as he approached Jericho, a blind man was sitting beside the road begging.
Hearing a crowd passing by, he asked what this might be.
They told him, “Jesus the Nazarene is passing by.”
He cried out, saying, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Those going ahead rebuked him so that he would be silent, but he cried out all the more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Jesus stopped and ordered that he be brought to him. When he came near, Jesus asked him,
“What do you want me to do for you?” He said, “Lord, that I may see again.”
Jesus said to him, “See again. Your faith has saved you.”
Immediately he received his sight and began following him, glorifying God. And when all the people saw it, they gave praise to God.
